title: Dynamic path-selection degradation playbook and follow-up actions
creator: Alex Kim
description: Summary: A subset of production inference requests experienced a sustained throughput regression after the dynamic path-selection heuristic rollout (runtime v1.17.2). Regression surfaced as 25–40% lower tokens/sec on certain long-context workloads. This ticket documents the investigation, temporary mitigations, and a concrete playbook + prioritized action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2024-11-08 we started seeing elevated per-request latency and throughput drops for customers using long sequence lengths (>2048) on the mL-large model family. Investigations tied the drop to an interaction between the new path-selection heuristic (which favors quantized kernels for memory and cost savings) and KV-cache warmup behavior: when cache misses coincided with selecting a less-efficient quantized kernel for particular attention patterns, the effective per-token throughput dropped significantly. Impact was medium: 3 enterprise customers reported degraded SLAs and internal dashboards showed 8% regional capacity stress.

root_cause: The dynamic path-selection heuristic relied on a simplified cost model that prioritized memory and static kernel speed benchmarks but did not properly account for the runtime cost of cold KV-cache misses and certain attention sparsity patterns. In production, when these conditions aligned, the heuristic selected quantized or tiled kernels that exhibited poor real-world throughput for the observed access pattern.
mitigations_taken: Hotfix v1.17.3: temporarily disabled quantized-preference rule for sequences >1024 on fleets serving mL-large
Traffic steering: routed high long-context customers to dedicated pools running baseline fused kernels for 48 hours
Instrumentation: added per-request kernel-choice and KV-cache-hit-rate logs to the tracing layer (flagged off by default)
postmortem_notes: This is not a single kernel bug but a cost-model mismatch between offline kernel benchmarks and online workload characteristics. The kernel implementations are healthy; the selection logic needs richer signals (live KV miss penalty, attention entropy, recent batching efficiency). We should treat the selection policy as a first-class system with test harnesses that simulate KV warmup and attention patterns.
proposed_action_items: (A1) Extend kernel selection cost model: add measured KV warmup penalty and attention-entropy term into scoring. Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2024-11-27

(A2) Add regression test harness: synthetic replay bench that exercises cold-cache sequences with varied attention sparsity and compares tokens/sec across kernel choices. Owner: Marcus Li. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2024-12-04
(A3) Canary policy flagging: require at least 72h canary with kernel-choice telemetry and automated rollback if throughput drops >10%. Owner: SRE-Oncall (rotation). Due: 2024-11-22
(A4) Dashboard: surface kernel-selection flip-rate and KV miss attribution per model family in Console -> Runtime Insights. Owner: Console PM (Riley Chen). Due: 2024-12-10

(A5) Experiment: run A/B of enhanced cost model on Dedicated pools with sampled customers to validate unit economics and latency SLOs before global rollout. Owner: Growth Eng (Aisha Gomez). Due: 2024-12-17

(A6) Documentation: update developer playbook with 'when to prefer fused baseline' guidance and a checklist for model onboarding to detect cold-cache sensitivity. Owner: Docs (Samira Khan). Due: 2024-11-30
